cards.explanation: The answer is John the Baptist. Some people say, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.” (Mark 6:14) Notice it's only what people are saying. Rumors travel fast, friends, and this one is about to land in the ear of a king.

The answer is brother. The text says Herod ordered John arrested “…on account of his brother Philip’s wife Herodias, whom Herod had married.” (Mark 6:17) So Philip, Herod's brother, was her husband first. I'd say that family tree needed a map.

The answer is that Herod has no right to marry Herodias. John had been telling Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife!” (Mark 6:18) He said it to a king's face. That took some courage, friends, and I can't even tell my own mustache to settle down.

The answer is False. John said, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife!” (Mark 6:18) Herodias did not shrug it off. She held a grudge and wanted to kill him (Mark 6:19). Some people let a thing go, and some people hold it tight.

The answer is that Herod feared John and protected him. Herod “…feared John and protected him, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man.” (Mark 6:20) So the same king who locked John up was also the one shielding him. I think that's a strange mix, and the text just lets it sit there.

The answer is True. Mark 6:20 says that when Herod heard John's words, “…he was greatly perplexed; yet he listened to him gladly.” Confused and still listening gladly. I know that feeling, like the time I read a recipe three times and still wasn't sure.

The answer is whatever she asks, up to half his kingdom. Herod swore to her, “Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, up to half my kingdom!” (Mark 6:23) He had already said she could ask for whatever she wished (Mark 6:22). That's a wide-open offer, friends, and an oath on top of it.

The answer is her mother Herodias. The girl went out and asked her mother, “What should I request?” (Mark 6:24) Herodias, the woman Herod had married, had held a grudge against John (Mark 6:19). I think this is the part where my own mustache goes still.

The answer is False. She did not take her time. “At once the girl hurried back to the king with her request…” (Mark 6:25) She even asked for it “immediately.” It's a heavy part of the story, friends, and the text shows how fast it moved.
The answer is sorrow. “The king was consumed with sorrow…” (Mark 6:26) That's a heavy moment, friends. He felt it, and the text tells us so.

The answer is because of his oaths and his guests. Mark 6:26 says, “The king was consumed with sorrow, but because of his oaths and his guests, he did not want to refuse her.” He had sworn in front of the leading men of Galilee (Mark 6:21-23). I think that's a sad thing to be stuck on, a promise made too fast.

The answer is True. The man “…brought John’s head on a platter and presented it to the girl, who gave it to her mother.” (Mark 6:28) This is one of the heaviest parts, friends. I think we can sit with that for a second.

The answer is that they took his body and laid it in a tomb. “When John’s disciples heard about this, they came and took his body and placed it in a tomb.” (Mark 6:29) After all that darkness, there are people who came to care for him. I think that's a quiet, faithful thing, friends, and I'm glad Mark tells us.
